name: POST /api/leadflow/intake/backfill - Drain the outage queue
description: Replays intake events parked while a downstream was unavailable, and reports how many drained and how many failed again. 200 rather than 201: a command against a queue, creating no addressable resource. Governed on data.configure, which is the point - a replay re-runs real side effects across routing, SLA clocks and notifications, and a rep working their own leads has no business triggering it. blockedOn narrows the drain to events parked on ONE dependency, so restoring a single connector does not replay everything parked for every other reason; omitting it drains all. The audit entry names the actor and what was drained, because a backfill nobody can attribute looks identical to a duplicate-send incident afterwards. QA: requiresRole admin, so the runner pre-fetches that identity and no Authorization header is declared here (MUST-71).

testCases.name: Drain only what was parked on one dependency
NEGATIVE: no Authorization header at all

errorCases.when: the Authorization header is absent, or present without a bearer token
the bearer token fails verification or has expired
the caller does not hold data.configure - a local 'user' account bridges to sales_rep, which does not
errorCases._whyNotReproducible: MUST-64/MUST-71: it needs a token from a DIFFERENT role, and this definition declares requiresRole so the runner pre-fetches the admin identity. Pinning a second Authorization alongside requiresRole is what MUST-71 forbids.
